Usage: gaia extract result [OPTIONS] TASK_ID

 Fetch what an LKM extraction task produced (GET /parse/task/{id}/result).

╭─ Arguments ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ *    task_id      TEXT  Extraction task id returned by `gaia extract         │
│                         submit`.                                             │
│                         [required]                                           │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
╭─ Options ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ --index,--server        TEXT  Configured LKM index id. [default: bohrium]    │
│ --out                   PATH  Write JSON to PATH (atomic) instead of stdout. │
│ --help                        Show this message and exit.                    │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

 The success payload is `variables` / `factors` / `motivations` / `stats`
 directly under `data` — not the `papers[]` wrapper `gaia search lkm package`
 returns, and not a nodes/edges graph. Every result also carries
 `step_durations`: how long each finished pipeline step took, in order.
 Node `local_id` values such as `paper:6::P1` are file-local. Only a non-null
 `global_id` is an LKM id you can pass to `gaia search lkm nodes` or `gaia pkg
 add`.
 Asking for the result of a queued or running task is a business error (code
 290017, exit 1); that does not mean the task was lost. Reviews and abstract
 collections often stop early, so an empty `files` list on a partial task is
 expected.
 API docs: https://s.apifox.cn/<UUID4>
